column2: Master of Advanced Studies in Climate Science and Policy
column47: The Master of Advanced Studies in Climate Science and Policy (MAS-CSP) is a one-year professional degree that gives students the knowledge they need to become leaders in the field of climate policy. Offered by Scripps Institution of Oceanography, the MAS-CSP curriculum is designed to teach students the fundamentals of climate science, how to evaluate the impacts of climate change, and how to effectively communicate and implement solutions. The program combines coursework from the physical, biological, and social sciences with professional training in communication and policy-making. Graduates of the MAS-CSP program are prepared to pursue careers in a wide array of fields, including government agencies, non-profits, and the private sector.

column2: Master of Science in Earth Sciences
column47: The Master of Science degree in Earth Sciences is a graduate program offered by the Earth Science program at Scripps Institution of Oceanography, in conjunction with the Graduate Division at UC San Diego. The program is designed for students who are interested in a terminal master’s degree with a focus in a specific area of Earth Sciences. The Earth Sciences M.S. degree provides a strong foundation for a variety of career pathways in industry, government, and education, and gives students the tools necessary to tackle a wide range of environmental problems. M.S. students will engage in a rigorous curriculum that includes quantitative coursework and training in computational analysis. The program also requires the completion of a capstone project which can be either a research-based thesis or a literature-based review paper on a topic of the student’s choosing, conducted under the supervision of a faculty advisor. The curriculum is intended to be completed in one year, but can be extended to two years for students with limited prior training in Earth Sciences.

column2: PhD in Earth Sciences
column47: The Geosciences of the Earth, Oceans, and Planets (GEO) curricular group at Scripps Institution of Oceanography encompasses a broad range of scientific disciplines focused on the Earth’s physical, chemical, and biological systems, from the deep interior to the oceans and atmosphere. Researchers in GEO study the fundamental processes that govern the evolution of the planet, the causes and consequences of natural hazards like earthquakes and volcanic eruptions, and the dynamics of the Earth’s climate system. The GEO curricular group emphasizes a multidisciplinary approach, combining field observations, laboratory experiments, and computational modeling to address some of the most pressing scientific questions of our time. Students in the GEO curricular group have the opportunity to work with leading experts in their fields, and to conduct research in some of the most remote and challenging environments on Earth. The GEO curricular group is also home to a number of world-class research facilities, including the Cecil H. and Ida M. Green Institute of Geophysics and Planetary Physics (IGPP), the Geosciences Research Division (GRD), and a number of analytical laboratories.

column47: The Interdisciplinary Environmental Research (PIER) Program is an optional specialization in the PhD program at Scripps Institution of Oceanography. PIER is designed to train a new generation of scientists and leaders to research and solve complex and interdisciplinary environmental problems. The PIER program provides an opportunity for students to specialize in a chosen field of research and to acquire the breadth and skills to work on problems that cross traditional disciplinary boundaries. Students gain this experience through a combination of interdisciplinary courses, seminars and colloquia, and an internship program that places them in a non-academic environment to gain experience in applying their knowledge. Admission to the PIER specialization is a two-step process. First, students must apply and be admitted to the PhD program at Scripps. Once accepted into the Scripps PhD program, students may apply to the PIER program for admission.

column2: PhD in Geophysics (Joint with San Diego State University)
column47: The Joint Doctoral Program in Geophysics with San Diego State University (SDSU) is a PhD program that operates under the framework of the existing Scripps Institution of Oceanography PhD program. Students have access to the broad resources of both institutions. In addition to a rigorous training in the fundamentals of geophysics, the program exposes students to a variety of research topics, and provides flexibility in designing a course of study that best suits their interests. Students interested in the Joint Program in Geophysics can apply through either UC San Diego or SDSU. Admission requirements are the same for both institutions and applications are evaluated by a joint admissions committee. Applicants are encouraged to contact potential advisors in their area of interest at either or both institutions.

column47: The Master of Advanced Studies (MAS) degree in Marine Biodiversity and Conservation (MBC) at Scripps Institution of Oceanography at UC San Diego is a 12-month, intensive program that is geared towards resource managers, environmental consultants, and informal science educators. Our goal is to train the next generation of leaders in marine conservation. This is accomplished through a comprehensive curriculum of interdisciplinary coursework and a collaborative, solution-based capstone project. In just one year, our students receive a broad introduction to the science, economics, and policy of marine conservation and gain practical skills to improve their effectiveness in the environmental arena.

column2: Master of Science in Marine Biology
column47: The master of science (M.S.) in marine biology is a two-year course of study that provides a broad, interdisciplinary education in marine biology. The M.S. degree is earned by the satisfactory completion of a minimum of 36 units of graduate coursework and the successful completion of a capstone requirement. The M.S. is considered a terminal degree at Scripps Institution of Oceanography, and students admitted to the M.S. program will not be able to transfer to the Ph.D. program. The marine biology M.S. degree is a Plan II (non-thesis) degree. The capstone requirement will consist of either: 1) a literature-based capstone paper and its defense at an oral examination, or 2) passing the Ph.D. departmental exam. Both options require an extensive literature review that demonstrates mastery of a specific area of marine biology. The capstone project must be completed by the end of the student’s second year of study.

column2: PhD in Marine Biology
column47: The Marine Biology PhD program at Scripps Institution of Oceanography is dedicated to training the next generation of leaders in marine biology science. Research in the Marine Biology PhD program at Scripps is managed through three multi-disciplinary research sections: Integrative Oceanography Division (IOD), Marine Biology Research Division (MBRD), and Center for Marine Biotechnology and Biomedicine (CMBB). Students are admitted into the PhD program and receive their degree through the Scripps Oceanography department. Marine Biology students are part of a unique department that houses a large diversity of scientific disciplines that all have in common a focus on the oceans. This allows for a truly interdisciplinary educational experience for our students. In addition to a broad suite of graduate courses in marine biology, students have access to courses in the other curricular programs at Scripps (Climate-Ocean-Atmosphere; Geosciences of the Earth, Oceans, and Planets; Ocean Biosciences) and in other departments at UC San Diego (e.g., Division of Biological Sciences, School of Medicine, Skaggs School of Pharmacy).

column2: PhD in Marine Biology with a Specialization in Interdisciplinary Environmental Research
column47: The Marine Biology PhD program at Scripps Institution of Oceanography is dedicated to training the next generation of leaders in marine biology and biological oceanography. Students are encouraged to develop their own research program from a wide range of fields including ecology, physiology, molecular biology, and symbiosis, applied to a diverse array of ocean ecosystems and organisms, ranging from microbes to whales. Marine Biology PhD students are based in two research sections at Scripps, Marine Biology Research Division (MBRD) and Integrative Oceanography Division (IOD). The core of the PhD curriculum is an interdisciplinary education in ocean sciences along with in-depth knowledge in marine biology and biological oceanography, and professional training in science communication, grant writing, teaching, and leadership. Students also have the option of pursuing a PhD specialization in Interdisciplinary Environmental Research. This specialization is for students interested in an interdisciplinary approach to research on environmental problems. Graduate students affiliated with PIER gain a broader perspective and a specialized skillset to tackle the world’s most challenging environmental problems.

column2: Master of Science in Oceanography
column47: The Master of Science in Oceanography at Scripps Institution of Oceanography is a terminal Master’s degree intended for students who have a strong science background and wish to get interdisciplinary training in oceanography. This degree provides students with knowledge of the diverse sub-disciplines of oceanography and the tools to succeed in a variety of related careers in industry, government, or education. The program takes between one to two years to complete. Students are required to take 36 units and complete a capstone project. Students work with a faculty advisor and a capstone committee to design and complete their project.

column47: The doctoral program in Anthropology at UC San Diego is one of the top programs in the country. We are ranked 6th in the nation in the most recent National Research Council (NRC) rankings of graduate programs. We are also ranked among the top programs by other measures, such as the number of federal grants received by our graduate students for their dissertation research. The department’s distinguished faculty is one of the most outstanding in the country in terms of its scholarly productivity and its success in training graduate students. We have a distinct profile in American anthropology due to the strong integration of its subfields—archaeological, biological, sociocultural, and linguistic anthropology—and its close ties with other disciplines, interdisciplinary programs and research centers across the campus. We admit a small, select group of students each year. This allows for close intellectual engagement between faculty and students.

column47: The Anthropological track of the Science Studies Program focuses on the ethnographic study of science, technology, and medicine. Anthropological science studies scholars analyze scientific and technical work where it happens -- in laboratories, clinics, and field sites -- as well as in the social worlds where scientific knowledge and technologies circulate. Anthropologists of science, technology, and medicine pay close attention to the ways in which local and global relations of power shape and are shaped by technoscience. The track brings these ethnographic sensibilities to the interdisciplinary field of science studies. Our faculty's expertise is global in scope, with particular strengths in Latin America, the United States, and Asia. Faculty and graduate students in the track are affiliated with a number of interdisciplinary programs on campus, including the Institute for Practical Ethics, the Center for Global Health, and Critical Gender Studies.

column2: PhD in Anthropology with a Specialization in Anthropogeny
column47:
The Anthropology Department, in collaboration with the Center for Academic Research and Training in Anthropogeny (CARTA) and the Salk Institute for Biological studies, offers a PhD in Anthropology with a Specialization in Anthropogeny. This specialization is designed to train graduate students in the transdisciplinary field of anthropogeny. Anthropogeny investigates the origin of humans. This is a vast and complex topic, requiring the integration of multiple disciplines from the social, behavioral, biomedical, and biological sciences.
The primary goals of this specialization are: To help students develop the ability to communicate across the different disciplines that contribute to anthropogeny. To provide a foundation of knowledge across these disciplines. To foster the transdisciplinary way of thinking that is necessary to fully explore the origin of humans.
Students will: Attend a three-quarter course sequence in anthropogeny. Participate in a quarterly CARTA-sponsored symposia series. Be eligible to receive fellowship support.

column2: PhD in Anthropology with a Specialization in Cognitive Science
column16: The UCSD Application for Graduate Admission is online. Applications are accepted for the PhD program for Fall quarter admission only. Applicants may apply to both the PhD program in Anthropology and the MAS program in the Anthropology of Climate Change. A separate application and fee are required for each program. Please review the Anthropology Graduate Admissions FAQs before applying. Required application materials for the PhD program include: the online application with application fee; statement of purpose; three letters of recommendation; a resume or curriculum vitae; a writing sample; transcripts from all post-secondary institutions attended; and TOEFL or IELTS scores for international applicants. The Department of Anthropology does not require GRE scores. For more detailed information on graduate admissions in Anthropology, visit the department website.
column47:
The Department of Anthropology, in conjunction with the Interdisciplinary PhD Program in Cognitive Science, offers a specialization in cognitive science for students in sociocultural, psychological, or biological anthropology. Anthropology is the study of human beings in the widest possible sense. It is a discipline that is global in its scope, historical in its depth, and holistic in its approach. Cognitive science is the interdisciplinary study of intelligent systems, both natural and artificial. It draws from anthropology, computer science, linguistics, neuroscience, philosophy, and psychology. The specialization in cognitive science is intended to provide anthropology students with a deeper understanding of the theories and methods of this allied discipline and to allow them to pursue research that crosses the boundaries between the two fields.

At the core of the specialization are two year-long proseminar courses that introduce students to the essential concepts and methods of cognitive science and a practicum in which students gain hands-on experience in the laboratory of a cognitive science faculty member. Additional advanced courses are available on a wide variety of topics. Students who complete the specialization will receive a parenthetical on their diploma: “PhD in Anthropology (with a Specialization in Cognitive Science).”

column47: Our doctoral program in Anthropology offers a rigorous training in the four sub-fields of the discipline: sociocultural, biological, and archaeological anthropology and anthropological linguistics. Although students are admitted to a specific sub-field, they are expected to gain a broad understanding of the whole discipline and to develop a research project of their own that may draw upon more than one sub-field. The first two years are spent in coursework, at the end of which students must pass a foreign language exam and write a second-year paper. After advancing to candidacy, by passing a qualifying exam, students carry out a major piece of independent fieldwork. The final stage of the program is the writing of a doctoral dissertation. While the department offers a focus in each of the four main sub-fields of anthropology, it is well known for a number of specializations that cut across these. These include: psychological anthropology, medical anthropology, the anthropology of modernity, the anthropology of religion, political anthropology, the anthropology of climate change, human-animal-environmental interactions, and the study of language in society.

column2: PhD in Anthropology with a Specialization in Interdisciplinary Environmental Research
column47: The Department of Anthropology at UC San Diego offers a program of graduate studies leading to the PhD degree. The Department has a distinctive profile within the discipline of anthropology. We are well-known as a department that is theoretically innovative and that bridges the traditional sub-fields of the discipline through an interdisciplinary and contemporary focus. We are committed to a comparative and critical understanding of what it is to be human in a complex and changing world. Our graduate curriculum reflects our department’s intellectual profile and commitment to holistic and integrated anthropology for the 21st century. The PhD program offers two specializations: Anthropogeny and Interdisciplinary Environmental Research. The Specialization in Interdisciplinary Environmental Research is designed for doctoral students who wish to communicate and collaborate with researchers across a wide range of academic disciplines in the natural sciences, physical sciences, social sciences, and humanities that are pursuing environmentally-focused research. The graduate Specialization in Interdisciplinary Environmental Research is a PhD specialization that may be taken in conjunction with any of the PhD degree programs at UC San Diego.

column2: PhD in Astronomy and Astrophysics
column47: The Astrophysics Ph.D. is an interdisciplinary program that includes researchers from the Department of Physics and the Center for Astrophysics and Space Sciences (CASS). CASS is one of the largest and most vibrant astrophysics groups in the world, with a broad range of research interests, including cosmology, galaxy formation, high-energy astrophysics, and exoplanets. Our astrophysics program emphasizes a broad education in fundamental physics as well as a focus on cutting edge research. Students are encouraged to get involved in research during their first year. Research at UC San Diego spans the full range of observational and theoretical astrophysics. We have a diverse faculty that actively participate in student mentorship. UC San Diego is a major partner in the Lick and Keck observatories, which ensures our students and faculty have guaranteed access to world-class facilities. We encourage you to browse our faculty page for more information on the research being carried out at UC San Diego. Our graduate students are also encouraged to interact with the broader San Diego astronomy community through events like the San Diego Astronomy Journal Club (SDAJC). For more information, please visit our prospective students page or attend one of our info sessions.

The program is designed to train audiologists to be leaders in the field and to provide the highest quality, evidence-based services to their patients. Graduates of our program are employed in a wide variety of clinical settings (e.g., hospitals, private practices, ENT offices), industry, and educational and research settings.

column47: The Department of Bioengineering offers a Master of Science (M.S.) degree in Bioengineering. This requirement is intended to provide a broad, graduate-level background in physiology, tissue engineering, and biomechanics. Beyond these core courses, M.S. students are encouraged to specialize by selecting a sequence of courses in their area of interest.

column2: Master of Science in Bioinformatics and Systems Biology

column47: The goal of the MS in Bioinformatics and Systems Biology is to train the next generation of scientists who are able to analyze large-scale biological and clinical data sets and to develop novel computational and mathematical approaches to solve pressing problems in biology and medicine. This MS program provides a rigorous, interdisciplinary training that combines coursework in biology, computer science, mathematics, statistics, and bioinformatics, with a thesis research project that will allow students to gain hands-on experience in cutting-edge research. The program prepares students for positions in the biotechnology and pharmaceutical industries as well as for entry into Ph.D. programs in bioinformatics and other related fields. The Bioinformatics and Systems Biology (BISB) MS degree program requires a minimum of forty-eight units of coursework, research, and a written thesis. The MS program takes approximately two years to complete, with a maximum time limit of three years.

The interdisciplinary nature of the program is ideal for students with undergraduate degrees in a wide range of fields, including biology, biochemistry, chemistry, computer science, mathematics, and bioengineering. The program aims to train the next generation of scientists who can bridge the fields of biology, medicine, and computer science and engineering; as such, we offer a rigorous and flexible curriculum that can be tailored to an individual student's interests. The program is committed to a culture of collaboration with students at the very core of our program. column2: Master of Science in Chemistry
column47:
The M.S. degree is offered with a major in chemistry. It is not required as a prerequisite for the Ph.D. degree. The M.S. degree in chemistry may be taken with one of three plans:
Plan I (Thesis): A minimum of 36 units of credit is required. At least 24 of these units must be in graduate-level courses. The remaining 12 units must be in upper-division (100-level) or graduate-level courses. A maximum of 12 of the 36 required units may be taken for a Satisfactory/Unsatisfactory grade. At least 12 of the 36 units must be in chemistry research (CHEM 299). A thesis is required. The thesis must be approved by a committee of three faculty members, and the student must pass an oral examination on the thesis research.
Plan II (Comprehensive Examination): A minimum of 36 units of credit is required. At least 24 of these units must be in graduate-level courses. The remaining 12 units must be in upper-division (100-level) or graduate-level courses. A maximum of 8 of the 36 required units may be taken for a Satisfactory/Unsatisfactory grade. No more than 4 of these units can be in non-letter graded research, CHEM 297 or CHEM 299. Satisfactory performance on a comprehensive examination is required.
Plan IV (Coursework): A minimum of 48 units of credit in upper-division (100-level) and graduate-level courses is required. At least 24 of these units must be in graduate-level chemistry courses, excluding special study (CHEM 296, 297, 299). A maximum of 8 units of upper-division courses may be taken in a related field. No units of research (CHEM 299) may be included in the 48 units of credit. Satisfactory performance on a comprehensive examination is required.

column47: The Master of Advanced Study (MAS) in Data Science and Engineering is designed to meet the needs of working professionals who want to develop deep expertise in data science and engineering to advance their careers. The MAS in Data Science and Engineering provides a rigorous, hands-on curriculum that encompasses both the principles of data science and the engineering skills needed to build and deploy large-scale data systems. Students will learn the latest techniques in machine learning, statistics, and data mining, as well as the fundamentals of data systems, including databases, distributed computing, and data visualization. Courses are offered in the evenings and on weekends to accommodate the schedules of working professionals. Students will have the opportunity to interact with leading researchers and practitioners in data science and engineering, and to network with other professionals in the field. The program is offered jointly by the Department of Computer Science and Engineering and the San Diego Supercomputer Center. Students will have access to the state-of-the-art computing resources of the San Diego Supercomputer Center, and will have the opportunity to work with real-world datasets from a variety of domains. The program prepares students for careers as data scientists, data engineers, and data analysts in a wide range of industries, including technology, finance, healthcare, and e-commerce. Graduates will be equipped with the skills and knowledge to design, build, and deploy data-driven solutions to the challenges of Big Data.

The Master of Science in Electrical and Computer Engineering (Advanced Manufacturing) program is a specialized professional master's degree program that prepares students for careers in this rapidly growing and dynamic field. Advanced manufacturing is an emerging field that requires significant interdisciplinary engineering training. The program is designed to attract and produce highly skilled engineers who are motivated to be the future leaders in the industry. It builds on the existing academic excellence of the UC San Diego Jacobs School of Engineering, and its close ties with the local and global manufacturing industry, and is a unique addition to the portfolio of engineering disciplines at UC San Diego.

The goal of this innovative program is to produce forward-thinking engineers who will be able to design, build, and manage the advanced manufacturing systems of tomorrow. These systems will rely on sophisticated automation and integrated information technologies that blur the line between bits and atoms. Students in the program will study at the intersection of information technologies, intelligent systems, sensing and control, and manufacturing practices. The curriculum includes four core courses that cover all aspects of advanced manufacturing: design, processes, automation, and supply chains. In addition, students have several technical electives to choose from to build technical depth in their areas of interest, such as additive manufacturing, advanced materials, robotics and automation, and supply chain management. The M.S. program also includes an invaluable internship with a local or global manufacturing company that will give students real-world experience.

column47: The Ph.D. program in Economics at UC San Diego is a 5-year program designed to train students to be professional economists. The department looks to admit 25-30 students per year. Our graduates have been very successful in securing excellent jobs. You can see a list of our initial placements for the last few years. The first year of the program is devoted to core classes in Macroeconomics, Microeconomics, and Econometrics. These classes provide the basic tools for all economists. At the end of the first year, students take qualifying exams in each of these three areas. In the second and third years, students take field courses to gain expertise in a smaller number of areas. A list of our fields can be found here. Starting in the summer after the first year, students will start working on their own research. The second year paper is due at the start of the third year. This is typically a student's first research paper and is a major requirement for the program. The third year paper is due at the start of the fourth year. This paper is also a major requirement for the program. The fourth and fifth years of the program are devoted to research for the dissertation. It is also informed by work in cognitive science, critical theory, cultural studies, discourse analysis, ethnic studies, language and linguistics, and sociolinguistics. The Ph.D. in Education prepares students to conduct research on the pressing educational issues of our time, and to bridge research and practice. In our program, you will develop the knowledge and skills necessary for a career in academia, in educational research, or in other leadership positions. All Ph.D. students specialize in one of three areas. They also must develop an interdisciplinary cognate by taking a series of courses outside of EDS.

column2: Master of Fine Arts in Theatre and Dance (Acting)
column16: In addition to the general admission requirements of the university, specific requirements for admission to the M.F.A. acting program are: an audition, three letters of recommendation (at least two from theatre professionals), a Statement of Purpose, a resume, and a recent photo.
column47: The MFA in Acting is a three-year program designed for the student-actor who has a desire to become a skilled professional actor on stage or screen. Students are trained by faculty artists and scholars with a wealth of experience in the professional world and in academia. The program offers a demanding and intensive journey of artistic exploration and development for a select group of students, with emphasis on individual growth and the creation of a strong ensemble. It culminates with a professional residency in the final quarter of the program, at La Jolla Playhouse. The training nurtures a well-rounded artist who will be prepared for a career in the professional theatre world, in a variety of performance mediums. UC San Diego is a NAST accredited program.

column2: Master of Fine Arts in Theatre and Dance (Dance Theatre)
column47: The MFA in Dance is a three-year program that offers graduate students the opportunity to concentrate on choreography and/or performance of contemporary dance. The curriculum supports the development of a strong personal artistic voice and an understanding of the artist's role in society. Courses in choreography, dance technique, performance, teaching, and dance studies are required. Students are provided with regular opportunities to create and show their work, and perform in faculty and student choreographed concerts. The program concludes with a final creative project, which can be a thesis performance of original choreography and/or a performance of a major role. Graduate students have the opportunity to serve as a Teaching Assistant, teaching classes in dance technique, dance studies and/or introductory courses for non-majors. This experience provides essential training for a career in academia.

column2: Master of Fine Arts in Theatre and Dance (Design)
column16: To apply to the Master of Fine Arts in Theatre and Dance (Design) program, applicants must complete the UC San Diego Online Application for Graduate Admission. column47:
The MFA Design Program at UC San Diego is a three-year program for students who intend to pursue a career as a professional designer in theatre, dance, or other live performance genres. The design program provides an environment where design faculty and students form a community of artists who work together and share a passion for the creation of new works. The program's proximity to a major theatre city allows for regular interaction with professional artists and theatres, which helps to foster an understanding of the current demands of the profession.

The curriculum is flexible and individually tailored, combining rigorous training with an emphasis on new work and new technology. Practical production work is an integral part of the graduate design training program, with each student designing in all four areas (costume, lighting, scenic, sound) for fully-mounted productions in the department's season. In addition, students will have the opportunity to serve as an assistant to a faculty or guest designer.

All graduate students have opportunities to collaborate on projects with MFA directors and playwrights, as well as with students from the PhD program in Theatre and Drama, a joint program with UC Irvine. Design students also collaborate with choreographers in the dance program.

column2: Master of Fine Arts in Theatre and Dance (Directing)
column47:
The three-year Directing program at UC San Diego is a selective and rigorous program dedicated to the artistic, intellectual and professional development of the emerging stage director.

Through a combination of seminars, studio classes, and a robust production season, directors will develop their individual voice and aesthetic while acquiring the necessary skills to lead a creative team through the process of making theatre.

Directors are guaranteed a production slot in the season in each of their three years. These projects are cast from the MFA acting cohort and are fully supported by the department's team of professional designers, stage managers and technicians.

In addition to the practical experience of directing in the season, students will assist faculty and guest directors on department productions, work as a teaching assistant for undergraduate courses, and may pursue independent study projects and internships with our professional theatre partners.

Directors will also have the opportunity to serve as producers of the annual Wagner New Play Festival, a department-wide celebration of new work by our graduate playwrights. In the Festival, each director will be paired with a playwright and will direct a workshop production of a new play.

At the conclusion of their third year, students will present their work in a showcase for industry professionals in Los Angeles and New York.

column2: Master of Fine Arts in Theatre and Dance (Playwriting)
column16:
All applicants, with the exception of joint doctoral program applicants, must submit the UC San Diego Application for Graduate Admission online. A non-refundable fee is required to submit the application. Please review the Graduate Division's website for Admissions requirements and information before applying.

Step-by-Step Application Instructions:
1. Complete the UC San Diego Application for Graduate Admission online.
2. Pay the non-refundable application fee.
3. Upload unofficial transcripts from all post-secondary institutions attended.
4. Complete the following sections of the UC San Diego Application for Graduate Admission:
   - Three Letters of Recommendation: Applicants are required to use the online application to submit letters of recommendation. Paper letters of recommendation will not be accepted.
   - Statement of Purpose: The Statement of Purpose should not be a reiteration of your C.V. or resume. It is a one-to-two-page essay that describes your past training and experience, your current artistic interests and focus, your reasons for applying to our MFA program, your long-term goals and what makes you a good candidate for our program.
   - Resume or C.V.
   - GRE: The GRE is no longer a requirement for admission to any of the graduate programs in the Department of Theatre and Dance.
   - TOEFL / IELTS: Required for international applicants only. The minimum TOEFL score required is 550 (paper-based) / 85 (internet-based). The minimum IELTS score is 7.
   - Program-Specific Requirements: Applicants to the Playwriting program are required to submit one full-length play as a writing sample. Plays should be a minimum of 60 pages in length. Please upload the writing sample as a PDF in the 'Playwriting Writing Sample' section of the online application.
column47:
The MFA playwriting program at UC San Diego is a three-year, intensive writing program. We only admit one or two writers a year. The small class size allows us to provide each writer with the individual attention his/her/their work requires. The program is committed to the idea that the theatre is a writer's medium and that the most exciting and vital theatre is created by artists who are passionate, disciplined and engaged in the world-at-large. Students write a full-length play each quarter. Each of these plays has at least a staged reading and some are given a workshop production. Every student will receive at least one production in the Wagner New Play Festival in the third year. All students are eligible to be chosen to receive a mainstage production in the department's subscription season.

The first year focuses on the fundamentals of dramatic writing through weekly writing assignments and the reading of a wide range of plays from the Greeks to the present day. The second year focuses on developing and deepening the writer’s voice and vision. In addition to playwriting workshops, seminars are offered in such subjects as theory and criticism, classical and contemporary drama, screenwriting and television writing, and teaching playwriting. Second- and third-year writers mentor undergraduate playwriting students. All playwriting students meet as a group once a week with the head of playwriting to discuss their work and other subjects of interest.

The UC San Diego Stage Management program is a three year, residency-based program designed to provide a select group of students with the opportunity to acquire the skills and training needed to become a leader in the theatre. It is a rigorous and comprehensive curriculum that combines classroom instruction with a strong emphasis on production work.

In the first year of training, students learn the fundamentals of stage management and serve as an assistant stage manager on at least two productions.

The second year focuses on honing the stage management skills of calling a show, managing a rehearsal room and functioning as the hub of communication. The second-year student will stage manage at least two productions.

Third year students stage manage one production and work on a professional residency at a theatre of their choice, such as La Jolla Playhouse or a regional theatre.

column2: PhD in Drama and Theatre with a Specialization in Critical Gender Studies (Joint with UC Irvine)
column47: The joint PhD program in Drama and Theatre between UC San Diego and UC Irvine offers students a unique course of study that combines the scholarly and pedagogical resources of two internationally-recognized departments and faculties. The program admits a small number of students each year for a curriculum that is designed to be completed in five years of residency. Students are typically admitted to and affiliated with a home campus, either UC San Diego or UC Irvine, and during their coursework they are in residence for one year at the other UC campus. During this year of residency, they take seminars, work with faculty and are fully integrated into the life of the other department. Courses on both campuses are available to all students in the program throughout their residency. The program is interdisciplinary in its orientation and it encourages students to develop a course of study that integrates the critical, historical, and theoretical dimensions of theatre and performance studies. The Department of Theatre and Dance is a participating department in the graduate specialization in Critical Gender Studies. The specialization provides specialized training in gender, sexuality, and queer studies for students currently enrolled in a UC San Diego doctoral program. The specialization is designed to complement students’ disciplinary training, introduce them to the central questions and methodologies of CGS as an interdisciplinary field, and provide a credential that will be legible to future employers. Admitted students are required to complete five courses (two core courses and three electives) and to include a chapter on a CGS-related topic in their doctoral dissertation. Upon successful completion of all requirements, students will receive a certificate of completion and the following notation on their transcript: 'Specialization in Critical Gender Studies.'

column47: The graduate program in History at UC San Diego is a vibrant intellectual community of faculty and students who share a commitment to historical research and analysis. Our distinguished faculty train graduate students to become scholars and teachers of the highest caliber. We offer programs of study leading to the Master of Arts (MA) and Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) degrees. Our areas of expertise include the history of the United States, Europe, Latin America, East Asia, the ancient Near East, the Middle East, and Science, Technology, and Medicine. The Department of History does not have a terminal M.A. program. The Master of Arts degree is awarded under one of three circumstances: 1. It is a prerequisite for doctoral candidates, and is based on a research paper (equivalent to a Master's Thesis) and a comprehensive written examination on a major and a minor field. 2. A student may be awarded a terminal master's degree in lieu of the PhD after successful completion of all requirements for the PhD except for the dissertation. 3. A terminal MA may be granted to students in the PhD program who for various reasons are not able to complete the doctoral degree.

column16: Admission to the Master of Public Policy (MPP) program is competitive. Applicants are evaluated based on their academic preparation, professional experience and demonstrated interest in public policy. While not all applicants will have had formal training in quantitative methods, we expect candidates to have an aptitude for analytical and quantitative work.

Our students learn to take on a broad range of policy challenges in the U.S. and around the globe. column2: Doctor of Education in Transformational Leadership (Ed.D.)
column47: The Joint Doctoral Program (JDP) in Educational Leadership at the University of California San Diego (UC San Diego) and California State University San Marcos (CSUSM) is a unique program that brings together the resources of two outstanding universities to offer a terminal degree in educational leadership. The program is designed to prepare a new generation of P-12 and postsecondary educational leaders who will be able to respond to the challenges of a pluralistic and globally-interconnected society. The Ed.D. in Transformational Leadership program offers students a timely, relevant and personalized experience. The program is designed for working professionals with a minimum of 5 years of leadership experience and uses a cohort model. Students begin the program each year in the summer and take classes for 3 consecutive years including summers.

column47: The Master of Arts in Latin American Studies is an interdisciplinary program designed to provide a broad-based, integrated understanding of contemporary Latin America. The program offers both a terminal M.A. degree for students who wish to pursue careers in the private or public sector, and a comprehensive M.A. for those who wish to continue their studies at the doctoral level. The program provides students with the intellectual tools for understanding the region, its people, and its cultures, as well as the challenges facing its societies. In the core curriculum, students study historical and contemporary issues facing Latin America from the perspectives of several different disciplines. They then select a disciplinary concentration (Anthropology, Communication, History, Literature, Political Science, Sociology) and a thematic focus (Cultural Studies, Gender Studies, International Migration, Public Health, or U.S.-Mexico Relations). Students may elect to pursue either Plan I (Thesis) or Plan II (Comprehensive Examination). Both are two-year programs. To earn the M.A. degree, students must demonstrate proficiency in Spanish or Portuguese, and complete a minimum of twelve courses (48 units). Students must receive a grade of B or better in all coursework to receive credit.

column2: Master of Arts in Linguistics

The program is designed to be a stepping stone to a PhD program in linguistics or a related field. It does not provide training for careers in translation, interpretation, or language teaching. The department does not offer a terminal M.A.

column47: The graduate program in linguistics at UC San Diego is a research-oriented program leading to the PhD degree. The department has a strong focus on theoretical linguistics, in the domains of syntax, semantics, phonology, and phonetics. The approach to linguistics is interdisciplinary, with an emphasis on the empirical foundations of linguistic theory. The department has a long-standing tradition of research in a wide variety of languages. Laboratory research is a key component of the doctoral program, with experimental work in phonetics, phonology, syntax, semantics, and language acquisition conducted in the department’s various labs. Students also have the option to pursue research on the linguistic structure of signed languages and on the neural bases of language. Close instructional and research connections exist with the Department of Cognitive Science, the Department of Communication, the Center for Research in Language, the Institute for Neural Computation, and the Salk Institute for Biological Studies. The interdisciplinary nature of research in linguistics is also supported by joint appointments of some Linguistics faculty in other departments, as well as through coursework and research opportunities in allied disciplines.

column2: Master of Arts in Literature
column47: The M.A. in Literature is a one-year degree that provides students an opportunity for concentrated study in a particular area of literature. The M.A. has three central components: a focused program of coursework, training in pedagogy, and a final portfolio project. Students may use the M.A. to prepare for a variety of professions, from teaching to publishing, or to prepare for applying to Ph.D. programs in literature and related fields. UCSD undergraduates may apply to our B.A./M.A. program.

column2: PhD in Literature
column47: The Literature Department at UC San Diego has from its beginning been committed to the study of literature and culture in a broad comparative and theoretical frame. Our graduate program is unique in its emphasis on historical and critical thinking and its attention to a wide range of languages and literatures. We do not have separate departments of English, Spanish, French, etc. Instead, our faculty is organized into language sections that include Chinese, English, French, German, Greek, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Latin, Russian, and Spanish. Our graduate students are also admitted into a language section where they are expected to do a substantial portion of their work. At the same time, we have a common curriculum for all students and faculty that is designed to train them as comparatists with a strong theoretical and historical grounding. Our focus on literary study is complemented by a rich and varied engagement with philosophy, history, and social and political thought, as well as with film and media studies, gender studies, and ethnic studies. This combination of linguistic rigor, comparative breadth, and theoretical sophistication has given our program a distinctive cast and a leading place in the country.

column2: Master of Science in Materials Science and Engineering
column47: The Materials Science and Engineering Program (MATS) at UC San Diego is an interdisciplinary program that offers M.S. and Ph.D. degrees in Materials Science and Engineering. The program brings together faculty from across the university, including the Departments of Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering, Structural Engineering, Electrical and Computer Engineering, NanoEngineering, Chemistry and Biochemistry, and Physics. Research in MATS focuses on the discovery of novel materials, and the understanding of the interrelationship between the selection, processing, structure, properties, and performance of materials, for the purpose of advancing engineering and scientific applications. MATS has strong interdisciplinary research collaborations, and has particular strengths in the following research thrusts: Advanced Structural Materials; Electronic and Photonic Materials; Energy Materials; Biomaterials and Soft Materials; and Computational Materials Science.

column2: PhD in Materials Science and Engineering
column47: The doctoral program in Materials Science and Engineering (PhD) is a research-oriented doctoral degree program. The program is designed to provide students with a solid foundation in the basic science of materials with opportunities to specialize in a particular area of materials science and engineering. Graduate students are trained for careers in academia, industry and national labs.

column2: Master of Arts in Mathematics
column47: The graduate program in mathematics at UC San Diego has, in its fifty year history, become a large and highly respected department. This is due to the high quality of the faculty and the students. The department has an international reputation for its work in a number of areas of both pure and applied mathematics. The department's graduate students are an important factor in its research life. Students are encouraged to become involved in research at an early stage. There are approximately one hundred fifty graduate students, and the small size of the advanced classes allows for a great deal of interaction between students and faculty. Students who perform well may be offered a teaching assistantship that provides a stipend and pays tuition and fees. Students from underrepresented groups who are U.S. citizens or permanent residents may be eligible for a San Diego fellowship. The department offers a terminal M.A. program with a specialization in statistics. Students in the M.A. program complete a set of qualifying exams for the Ph.D. program and then follow a course of study which enables them to write a thesis (Plan I) or take a comprehensive examination (Plan II). The M.A. programs prepare students for careers in government and industry, for teaching at the community college level, and for further study at the doctoral level in pure or applied mathematics.

The M.S. degree is offered in three specializations: Mathematics, Applied Mathematics, and Statistics. We offer two plans for the M.S. degree: Plan I (Thesis) and Plan II (Comprehensive Exam). column47: The graduate program in mathematics at UC San Diego has been ranked 19th among public universities and 34th overall among U.S. universities by U.S. News & World Report. The department faculty includes many pre-eminent mathematicians who have been recognized for their research by professional societies, prestigious fellowships, and other honors. The graduate program provides a rich and rewarding experience in a beautiful Southern California setting. With five required first-year courses in algebra, analysis, and topology, the program ensures students have a strong, broad foundation in mathematics. The remaining curriculum is flexible and can be tailored for each student's interests and goals. Students are encouraged to attend a variety of research seminars, starting in their first year. After passing the qualifying exams (typically in the second year), students begin to work closely with a faculty advisor. The department has active research groups in most areas of mathematics, including algebra, analysis, combinatorics, geometry, logic, number theory, numerical analysis, probability, and statistics.

column47: The UC San Diego School of Medicine MD degree program is a four-year program that provides comprehensive education in the art and science of medicine. In the pre-clerkship phase, students learn the foundational sciences of medicine, including anatomy, biochemistry, and physiology. In the clerkship phase, students rotate through various clinical specialties, such as internal medicine, pediatrics, and surgery.

column47: The graduate program in music at UC San Diego offers the degrees of Doctor of Philosophy (Ph.D.) and Master of Arts (M.A.). The program is highly selective. It is not our goal to produce a large number of graduates but to provide an environment in which a few gifted individuals can pursue their musical interests and develop their skills to the fullest. We are interested in students who have already demonstrated significant achievement and who are dedicated to a life of continuing artistic and intellectual growth. The M.A. is a two-year degree with concentrations in Composition, Computer Music, or Integrative Studies. The M.A. program is designed for students who have not yet had sufficient background and training to be admitted to the Ph.D. program. The M.A. is also appropriate for those who wish to pursue a more limited course of study beyond the bachelor’s degree. Students are admitted to one of the three areas of concentration listed above.

column47: The Doctor of Musical Arts (DMA) in Contemporary Music Performance is offered by the Department of Music at UC San Diego. The program is unique in that it is a research-oriented doctoral program in performance, designed to be on a par with the Ph.D. The program aims to produce performers who are also scholars and scholar-performers who are also outstanding musicians. The program is intentionally small to allow for intensive contact between students and faculty. The department has a large and varied faculty in performance who work in a variety of musical styles with emphasis in contemporary music. Most performance faculty perform in the top professional new music ensembles in the San Diego area, including the San Diego Symphony, or are active as soloists and chamber musicians nationally and internationally. The program gives students a strong technical foundation on their instrument, experience in a wide range of repertoire, and the development of a personal artistic vision through in-depth study of music of the 20th and 21st centuries. Students will gain experience in a variety of performance situations, from solo and chamber music to large ensemble, and will be given opportunities to work with composers and to participate in the creation of new works. Students will have access to a wide variety of courses in the Department of Music, including courses in composition, computer music, and integrative studies.

column2: PhD in Music

column46: Composition, Computer Music, Integrative Studies, Performance
column47: The Ph.D. program in Music is an integrated degree with five specialized areas of study, referred to as 'research areas': Composition, Computer Music, Integrative Studies, and Performance. It is a fundamental feature of the Department that these research areas are not separate departments, but interact on a daily basis. The focus of the program is on the creation of new music and the development of new ideas about music. Music at UCSD is understood to be an art of sound, and all sound is considered potential material for musical creation and inquiry. We do not privilege any one style or tradition of music making or study, and we encourage our graduate students to explore the rich variety of musics available to them. To this end we offer a strong faculty representing a wide array of musical interests. Our goal is to prepare graduate students to be the next generation of composers, performers, and scholars who will lead the field in the twenty-first century.

column2: PhD in Neurosciences
column16: Applicants are asked to submit a statement of purpose that describes their past research experience, their future research interests, and their motivation for pursuing a Ph.D. in neurosciences. We recommend that applicants also identify several faculty members whose research they find particularly interesting. Applicants are asked to provide three letters of recommendation from individuals who are in a position to analyze their academic ability and research potential. These letters should be from faculty and/or supervisors who are familiar with the applicant's research experience. Applicants are asked to submit a resume or curriculum vitae that outlines their academic and research background.
column47: The Neurosciences Graduate Program at UC San Diego is an inter-institutional program dedicated to training the next generation of leaders in neuroscience research, education, and outreach. The program spans more than 30 departments and sections across UC San Diego and three affiliated research institutes: the Salk Institute for Biological Studies, the Sanford Burnham Prebys Medical Discovery Institute, and The Scripps Research Institute. Established in 1968, the program is the oldest and one of the largest neuroscience graduate programs in the country. Our more than 160 faculty provide an extraordinary breadth of research and training opportunities, in a collaborative and collegial atmosphere. Students receive five years of guaranteed financial support and typically complete their PhDs in an average of 5.5 years. The program is committed to a holistic admissions process, recognizing that a diverse and inclusive student body is a cornerstone of a preeminent graduate program.

A bachelor's degree is not required for admission, however, applicants must have a cumulative GPA of a 3.0 or above and have completed the required prerequisite courses from a U.S. accredited college or university. column38: Skaggs School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
column47: The Skaggs School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences at UC San Diego offers a four-year Doctor of Pharmacy (Pharm.D.) degree program that is committed to providing an innovative and flexible curriculum in a highly inter-disciplinary environment. The curriculum is taught by a unique blend of faculty from the School of Pharmacy, the UC San Diego School of Medicine and other campus departments. The program focuses on the students' development as future leaders in pharmacy by providing opportunities for inter-professional collaborations in patient care, leadership roles in professional organizations, and specialized elective streams that are tailored to the students' career goals. The small class size, paired with San Diego's collaborative biotech and medical environment, allows for a personalized and team-oriented experience which prepares students to be successful leaders in patient care, research, and industry.
column50: The University of California San Diego Skaggs School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences’ Doctor of Pharmacy program is accredited by the Accreditation Council for Pharmacy Education, 190 South LaSalle Street, Suite 3000, Chicago, IL 60603, 312/664-3575; FAX 866/228-2631, web site www.acpe-accredit.org.

column2: Master of Science in Pharmaceutical Sciences

column47: The Master of Science in Drug Development and Product Management is a one-year, in-person master’s degree program that provides students with a multidisciplinary education to meet the needs of the pharmaceutical industry. The program is specifically designed to provide students with the key knowledge and skills that are essential to transition to a career in drug development and product management. Students will learn the process of how a drug or a product moves from the laboratory to the marketplace from world-renowned faculty at the University of California San Diego. Students will also experience hands-on training via the capstone course where they will learn from and interact with industry leaders in drug development, clinical trials, business development and project management. The curriculum also provides students with the training in professional development to support successful career placement following graduation.

column2: PhD in Pharmaceutical Sciences
column38: Skaggs School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
column47: The Skaggs School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences offers a PhD degree program in Pharmaceutical and Biomedical Sciences. The doctoral degree program provides a strong foundation in the fundamental principles of drug discovery, drug delivery and drug action, and prepares students for a variety of careers in academia, the pharmaceutical and biotech industries, as well as government. The curriculum is interdisciplinary, offers training in diverse areas of pharmaceutical and biomedical sciences, and fosters collaborations between students and faculty in different specializations. The Skaggs School of Pharmacy is part of UC San Diego Health Sciences, which also includes the School of Medicine, the Wertheim School of Public Health and Human Longevity Science, and UC San Diego Health. UC San Diego Health Sciences is an innovative, collaborative, and highly translational environment for biomedical research.

column16: Applicants for admission to the MA program should have an undergraduate major in philosophy or an equivalent set of courses in the discipline. column47: The department offers a terminal M.A. program in philosophy. The M.A. is designed to be completed in one year (three quarters) of full-time study. The program is designed for students who can benefit from a year of graduate-level work in philosophy. Some students enter the program to deepen their knowledge of philosophy before applying to Ph.D. programs, while others are interested in the connections between philosophy and their undergraduate major or profession. Still others are drawn to the program out of an interest in philosophy and a desire to pursue it at a more advanced level. The M.A. program has been very successful at preparing students for admission to Ph.D. programs in philosophy. In recent years, our M.A. students have been admitted with multi-year funding packages to Ph.D. programs at Brown University, Columbia University, Cornell University, the University of Michigan, the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, Princeton University, the University of Southern California, Stanford University, the University of Texas at Austin, and the University of Wisconsin-Madison, among many others. The M.A. program draws on the same faculty and graduate seminars as our Ph.D. program, and M.A. students are integrated into the regular life of the department.

column47: The graduate program in philosophy at UC San-Diego is a Ph.D. program. The department offers a broad range of courses, a distinguished and dedicated faculty, a diverse and excellent group of graduate students, and a supportive intellectual environment in which to pursue graduate work. The program is designed to be completed in five years. The curriculum is flexible, designed to allow students to develop their own interests, while at the same time insuring that they receive a solid grounding in the core areas of philosophy.

column47: The Department of Physics offers a terminal M.S. program for students wishing to obtain a master's degree before pursuing a career in industry, business, education, or government. column47: The UC San Diego Department of Physics offers a comprehensive Ph.D. program that prepares students for careers in academia, industry and national laboratories. At the same time, students are encouraged to get involved in research within the first year by participating in research projects with our faculty. After passing a qualifying exam based on core graduate course material, students focus on their Ph.D. research. All of our Ph.D. students are supported as teaching assistants or research assistants during their graduate career. They write a significant research paper as their capstone experience. The program provides the intellectual and analytic tools for a professional career in public service, government, or the private sector. It can also serve as a foundation for further graduate study at the Ph.D. level.

column2: PhD in Political Science
column47: The graduate program in Political Science at the University of California San Diego is a top-ranked program that provides doctoral students with the theoretical and methodological skills to conduct high-quality, cutting-edge research. The Department of Political Science offers the Ph.D. in four primary fields of study: American Politics, Comparative Politics, International Relations, and Political Theory. We also offer a secondary concentration in Methodology. Our students work closely with world-renowned faculty who are leading scholars in their fields. The program is designed to prepare students for careers in academia, research, and public service.

column47: The joint Ph.D. in Political Science and International Affairs is a collaboration between the Department of Political Science in the School of Social Sciences and the School of Global Policy and Strategy (GPS). It is designed to join the department’s expertise in political science research with GPS's regional and multidisciplinary expertise. Students in the joint program pursue a Ph.D. in political science with a special emphasis in international affairs. All students in the program take the political science courses required for a Ph.D. in political science. Students also complete a set of core courses at GPS in international relations, policy analysis, finance and management, and quantitative methods. Joint program students must have a regional concentration. Available regions are Latin America, Southeast Asia, Northeast Asia, and China. Students take at least four courses in their regional concentration area. The dissertation for a student in the joint program must be on a topic in international affairs.

column47: The Master of Public Health (MPH) is a professional degree that provides a population-based perspective and is designed to prepare students to investigate and manage public health problems. The MPH program provides grounding in the foundational public health knowledge, in addition to concentration-specific knowledge, that will enable them to apply public health principles to a variety of settings. Students learn about the social and behavioral sciences, epidemiology, biostatistics, environmental health, and health services administration as well as their application to public health problems. Through a combination of coursework, a hands-on applied practical experience, and a capstone project, students learn to apply public health principles to real-world problems. MPH graduates go on to careers in a wide range of fields in both the public and private sectors.

This unique doctoral program, also known as the Joint Doctoral Program (JDP) in Public Health, provides rigorous training for future leaders in public health. Students in the PhD program have the opportunity to specialize in one of four concentrations: Epidemiology, Global Health, Health Behavior, or Public Mental Health.

The program provides students with a strong academic foundation in the core disciplines of public health, in-depth training in one of the specialized areas of concentration, and the skills needed to conduct independent, interdisciplinary research. Graduates from this program are prepared for leadership roles in academic institutions, public health agencies at the local, state, federal, and international levels, and in the private sector.

The M.S. degree is earned with the completion of 40 units of coursework, a major paper, and a comprehensive exam. It is a one-year program with courses that introduce students to the key ideas and debates in sociology and provide them with the skills to conduct their own research. Students will have the opportunity to work closely with faculty members who are leaders in their fields, and to develop their own research interests. The program is ideal for students who want to pursue a career in research, policy, or the non-profit sector, as well as for those who want to continue on to a Ph.D. program in sociology or a related field.

column2: Master of Fine Arts in Visual Arts
column47:
The MFA program in Visual Arts is a two-to-three-year, studio-based course of study for artists. The program is unique in that it encourages a diversity of art practices and allows for a wide range of explorations in a climate of critical exchange. The department promotes intensive inquiry, and students are encouraged to engage in a manner of working that is thoughtful, rigorous, and adventurous. Faculty and students have at their disposal first-rate facilities, and through a program of visiting artists and critics, students are consistently exposed to a wide variety of contemporary art practices and perspectives. The small size of the program, with an average of eight new students admitted each year, allows for an intimate environment, fostering a vibrant and supportive community among the students and faculty alike.
The MFA program is a two-year program (although up to three years of residency is permitted, with normative time being two years). It requires a total of 72 units for the degree. At least 50% of the course work must be at the graduate level in the department of Visual Arts. Course work is determined in consultation between the student and their faculty advisor. While the curriculum is highly individualized, students are required to complete a minimum number of credits in the following areas: Graduate Studio (VIS 201-209), Visual Arts Seminar (VIS 219), Art Practice Graduate Seminar (VIS 220), one course in art history/theory/criticism at either the graduate or upper-division undergraduate level, and the First & Final Year MFA Reviews (VIS 297 & VIS 298).

column47: The Ph.D. Program in Art History, Theory, and Criticism is a multi-faceted program that offers students a combination of carefully guided research and intellectual debate. Students follow a course of study that combines a broad education in the history and theory of art with a specific focus on an area of specialization. With a core of Art History faculty, and a large group of affiliated faculty, the program offers a wide range of fields of study. These include Ancient, Medieval, Renaissance, Early Modern and Modern European and American Art, Pre-Columbian and Latin American Art, and the Arts of China and Japan. In addition, students have the option to engage in interdisciplinary research on topics in art theory and criticism, and architectural history and theory, drawing on the expertise of faculty in the departments of History, Literature, Ethnic Studies, Anthropology, Communications and the School of Global Policy and Strategy. The Art Practice concentration provides an alternative to the traditional art history Ph.D. for a select group of students who, in addition to their scholarly work, are also practicing artists. The Art Practice concentration seeks to create a new generation of artists/scholars who are uniquely equipped to meet the challenges of art practice and education in the 21st century. The concentration combines the curriculum of the Ph.D. in Art History, Theory, and Criticism with the curriculum of the M.F.A. in Visual Arts. The concentration offers Ph.D. students the opportunity to complement their scholarly research with a strong studio component that includes graduate-level art-making seminars, and independent studies with the department’s renowned studio faculty. Students in the Art Practice concentration are expected to produce an ambitious body of artwork as their dissertation.

column2: Certificate in Business Administration
column47: The Certificate in Business Administration is a four-course program that provides students with the fundamental building blocks of a business education. The program is designed for working professionals, recent graduates and international students who are looking to advance their careers or pursue a graduate business degree. The program gives students an in-depth understanding of the core disciplines of business and the opportunity to focus their studies in a particular area of business. The program offers two tracks: General Business Administration and Technology Management. The program covers a variety of topics and prepares students to face the challenges of today's fast-paced, global marketplace.

column2: Certificate in Business Management
column47: The Business Management Certificate is a part-time program for professionals who want to strengthen their knowledge of key business functions. This program is for individuals who do not have an undergraduate degree in business, but want to gain business skills to pursue an MBA or a management position. This certificate is also ideal for professionals seeking a career change and entrepreneurs who have a business idea and want to gain a deeper understanding of business fundamentals. In this certificate program, you will develop a fundamental understanding of business concepts and practices. You will learn about managerial accounting and finance, marketing principles and supply chain management. This program also fulfills many of the prerequisites needed to apply for the Rady School’s MBA programs.

column2: Certificate in Digital Marketing
column47: The Digital Marketing certificate is a comprehensive program that provides you with tactical knowledge in various digital marketing disciplines. The curriculum focuses on SEO, content marketing, paid search, social media, conversion optimization, web analytics, mobile marketing, and email marketing. Whether you are a business owner looking to grow your business online, a traditional marketing professional looking to upskill, or a beginner looking to launch a new career in marketing, the Digital Marketing certificate is designed to provide you with a strong foundation to grow your business and your career. Upon completion of this certificate, you will be able to develop and implement a successful digital marketing strategy.
column50: UC San Diego Extended Studies is accredited by the Western Association of Schools and Colleges (WASC).

column2: Certificate in Leadership and Management
column47: The Gordon Engineering Leadership Center offers a depth and breadth of leadership courses that allow our engineering students to develop the skills needed to become tomorrow's engineering leaders. The Bernard and Sophia Gordon Engineering Leadership Center is the first undergraduate engineering leadership center in the nation. It was established with the mission to educate and train effective engineering leaders who are capable of developing new products and services for the good of society. The Certificate in Leadership and Management will give students the opportunity to learn and practice the leadership and management skills required to be an effective engineering leader. The goal of this certificate is to develop students into future engineering leaders by providing them with the necessary skills to lead and manage engineering teams and projects. The certificate prepares students for their future leadership roles in the industry by exposing them to leadership frameworks, project management techniques, business and innovation principles, and team engineering best practices.

column2: Certificate in Project Management
column47: The Master of Advanced Studies (MAS) in the Architecture-based Enterprise Systems Engineering (AESE) program, offered by the Jacobs School of Engineering in collaboration with the Rady School of Management, is a graduate degree program designed for working professionals. The MAS-AESE degree has an option of a specialization certificate in Project Management, which is a graduate-level certificate program designed to provide students with advanced education in the art and science of project management. The curriculum provides a primary emphasis on the systems engineering and business aspects of managing complex projects. The program will equip students with knowledge and skills to become future leaders in project management.

It leverages and complements the core MS/PhD curriculum in MAE by providing training in state-of-the-art topics that are highly sought by employers in the energy and technology sectors.
